info.title: Apelora control plane API
info.description: Inventory, audit and identity for an Apelora fabric. Inventory responses name their source (mock or Incus) and when they were observed.

get.summary:
Applications the caller may see, each with design status, derived runtime status, replica
health, and the actions they may take now. Needs `application.view`.

post.summary:
Creates an application in an environment, optionally with its first draft. Needs
`application.create` on the environment's project.

get.summary:
One application with its modules (desired and observed), versions and recent operations.
Needs `application.view`.

patch.summary: Changes an application's description or icon (its name cannot change). Needs `application.design`.

get.summary:
What the caller may open on each instance of the application now, with the reason when not.
This is the source for the interface's menu entries. Needs `application.view`.

post.summary:
Archives an application that is not running; it leaves the default list and keeps its data.
Needs `application.delete`.

Deploys the design: saves it as a new revision and queues the planned changes. Refuses
the whole deployment if any module conflicts with an existing instance. Needs `deploy`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes the request safe to repeat

get.summary: The application's working document. 404 when it has none yet. Needs `application.view`.

put.summary:
Saves the draft as the next version. Refused with 409 `draft_conflict` (and the current
version) when someone saved since `baseVersion`; nothing is overwritten. Needs `application.design`.

get.summary:
What happened to the application: creation, saves, versions, deployments, operations,
refusals. Needs `application.view`.

post.summary:
Opens a session: checks the caller, the instance and the approval rule, and answers with a
single-use ticket for the websocket. Needs `instance.console` (terminal, PowerShell) or
`instance.desktop` (RDP) on the application; in production also an approval
(`Apelora-Approval: <id>`) of `instance.console` on `instance:<application>/<instance>`.

get.summary: Recent operations of the application, newest first. Needs `application.view`.

post.summary:
Starts, stops or restarts the application's instances, in dependency order, as an
asynchronous operation. Succeeds only when Incus confirms each instance's state. Needs
`application.operate` on the application. It only touches instances this application owns;
networks, volumes, data and other applications are left alone.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes the request safe to repeat

get.summary: One operation with the progress of each phase and instance. Needs `application.view`.

post.summary: What deploying the design would change, without changing anything. Needs `deploy`.
Brings an archived application back. Needs `application.delete`.

get.summary: The application's instances as Incus reports them, by module. Needs `read-inventory`.
Versions of the application, newest first. Needs `application.view`.

post.summary:
Releases the current draft as the next immutable published version. Refused while the draft
is invalid or when this draft version is already published. Needs `application.design`.

get.summary: The document of one version. Needs `application.view`.
The application's volumes, with what Incus says about each now. Needs `application.view`.

delete.summary:
Deletes one of the application's volumes and its snapshots, for good. The volume's Incus
name must be typed again; refused while an instance uses it. Needs `application.delete`
(and an approval where the policy asks for one); audited.

patch.summary:
Grows one of the application's volumes, also while its instance runs. Volumes only grow:
a smaller size is refused. Needs `application.deploy`; audited.

get.summary: The volume's snapshots, oldest first. Needs `application.view`.

post.summary:
Takes a snapshot of the volume, named after the time (`snap-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS`). While an
instance runs the snapshot is only crash-consistent; the response says which. Snapshots
are not backups: they live in the same pool. Needs `application.operate`; audited.

delete.summary: Deletes one snapshot of the volume. Needs `application.delete`; audited.

post.summary:
Puts the volume back to a snapshot: everything written since is lost. The snapshot's name
must be typed again, and every instance using the volume must be stopped. Needs
`application.operate` (and an approval where the policy asks for one); audited.

get.summary: Requests and approvals: your own, plus every open one if you may approve. Needs `approval.request` or `approval.grant`.

post.summary:
Asks for approval of one risky action on one target. You must be allowed to do the action
yourself; someone else with `approval.grant` then decides. Needs `approval.request`.
Approves a request made by someone else. Needs `approval.grant`. The approval is good for 30 minutes, once.
Withdraws your own pending request. Needs `approval.request`.
Rejects a request. Needs `approval.grant`.

get.summary:
The most recent audit events the caller may read, newest first. Needs `audit.read`
(platform-wide, or limited to the events of the caller's organisations, projects and
applications) and a database.
The Incus server and its cluster members. Needs `read-inventory`.
Join tokens waiting to be used (no secrets). Needs `manage-infrastructure`.

post.summary:
Approves a new cluster member: asks Incus for a single-use join token. Needs
`manage-infrastructure`. The token is in this response only.

delete.summary:
Withdraws a new member's approval: revokes its unused join token. Needs
`manage-infrastructure`.

parameters.name: member
parameters.description: Name the token was issued for

post.summary:
Evacuates a cluster member through Incus after re-running the dry run: refused while
anything blocks it. Needs `manage-infrastructure` and the admin identity; audited.

get.summary:
Dry run of evacuating a cluster member: per instance, what Incus will do and what it means
for the application; what blocks it; what to accept. Changes nothing.

Dry run of removing a cluster member for good: what is still on it, what blocks it and what
to accept. Changes nothing.

post.summary:
Removes an evacuated, empty member from the cluster for good, after the check runs again:
refused while anything blocks it. Needs `cluster.manage`, the admin identity and the
member's name typed again; audited.

Restores an evacuated member: Incus moves its instances back and starts them. Needs
`manage-infrastructure` and the admin identity; audited.

get.summary:
Public. Reports the service, the inventory provider, the authentication mode and whether
Incus is reachable.
Role assignments in the caller's scopes. Needs `user.view`.

post.summary:
Grants a role to a person, group or automation identity at a scope. Needs `role.assign` there
and every permission the role holds (no escalation); audited.

Shows what an assignment would give before it is saved: what the person can already do at the
scope, what they could do afterwards, which permissions would be inert, and whether you may
save it. Changes nothing. Needs `role.assign`.

delete.summary:
Revokes an assignment; the person loses it on their next request. Needs `role.assign` in its
scope. The last platform super admin cannot be revoked.

get.summary: Audit history the caller may read, filtered and paged. Needs `audit.read`.

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only actions starting with this, e.g. `role.` or `emergency_access.`.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only events older than this id (paging).

post.summary:
Grants a person a platform role for a short time, with a recorded reason (break-glass). You
cannot grant it to yourself; every request made with it is audited. Needs `platform.emergency_access`.

get.summary: Groups the caller may see. Needs `user.view`.

post.summary:
Creates a group: an organisation's (needs `group.manage` there) or a platform group (platform
`group.manage`). Mapping a group to an identity-provider group name is platform-only.

get.summary: Members of a group. Needs `user.view` or `group.manage` on the group's organisation.

put.summary: Adds a person to a group. Needs `group.manage`.

delete.summary: Removes a person from a group; their access through it ends on their next request. Needs `group.manage`.

get.summary: Organisations the caller may see. Needs `organization.view` (or a grant below that reaches them).

post.summary: Creates an organisation. Needs `organization.create` (platform).
Creates a project in an organisation. Needs `project.create` on the organisation.

get.summary: Every permission, its class and the narrowest scope at which a grant takes effect.
Access policies (MFA and approval rules). Needs `access_policy.manage` or `audit.read`.

put.summary:
Creates or updates a policy by name. `mfa`: `{"environments": ["production"], "infrastructure": true}`.
`approval`: `{"actions": ["cluster.evacuate"]}` (extra actions that need approval where the API
already asks for it). Needs `access_policy.manage`.

get.summary: Projects the caller may see, optionally of one organisation. Needs `project.view`.
Environments of a project. Needs `project.view` on it.

post.summary:
Creates an environment. The Incus project it maps to is derived from the names (tenants cannot
choose it); platform administrators may map an existing one. Needs `environment.manage`.

get.summary: The predefined and custom roles with their permissions.

post.summary:
Defines a custom role from explicit permissions. Needs `role.manage` (platform), and you may
only include permissions you hold yourself.

delete.summary: Deletes a custom role that no assignment uses. Needs `role.manage`.

get.summary:
Registered service identities (the credentials Apelora uses for Incus and MAAS, and automation
identities that call this API). Needs `service_identity.manage`.

post.summary:
Registers a service identity. Outbound kinds (workload, network, storage, provisioning) record
only the name of a credential held in the secret store; automation identities get an API token,
shown once. Needs `service_identity.manage`.
Disables a service identity at once. Needs `service_identity.manage`.
Re-enables a service identity. Needs `service_identity.manage`.

get.summary:
People who have signed in, as far as the caller may see them: everyone for a platform
administrator, otherwise those with a role in the caller's scopes. Needs `user.view`.

Finds one person by exact user name or e-mail so a role can be given to them. Someone who has
never signed in does not exist yet. Needs `role.assign` or `group.manage`.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Exact user name or e-mail address.

post.summary: Disables a person: their tokens stop working at once. Needs `user.manage`.
Re-enables a person. Needs `user.manage`.

get.summary: Instances in all projects. Needs `read-inventory`.

post.summary:
Queues creation of an instance. Needs `deploy`. Apelora marks it as its own; only such
instances can later be stopped or deleted through Apelora.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes the request safe to repeat

delete.summary: Queues deletion of an Apelora instance (stopped first if running). Needs `deploy`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes the request safe to repeat

get.summary:
Dry run of moving an instance to another member: whether it keeps running, what it copies,
what blocks it. Changes nothing. Needs `deploy` (or `instance.manage`).

parameters.name: allowStop
parameters.description: Whether a short stop is acceptable when it cannot move while running.

post.summary:
Moves an Apelora instance to another member, after the check runs again and its name is
typed: live when it can, otherwise only with `allowStop`, copying its volumes there.
Queues an `instance.move` job. Needs `deploy` (or `instance.manage`); audited.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes the request safe to repeat

post.summary: Queues starting or stopping an Apelora instance. Needs `deploy`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes the request safe to repeat

get.summary: The 100 most recent jobs, newest first. Needs `read-inventory`.
A queued job and its progress. Needs `read-inventory`.
Machines being enrolled, with their state derived from Incus. Needs `manage-infrastructure`.

post.summary:
Registers a machine. A name that is already an eligible member is adopted as admitted.
Needs `manage-infrastructure`; audited.

delete.summary:
Forgets a machine that is not a cluster member (revoking an unused join token). Needs
`manage-infrastructure`; audited.

get.summary:
The admission checks for a joined machine (dry run; changes nothing). Needs
`manage-infrastructure`.

post.summary:
Admits a joined machine: re-runs the admission checks and, when none fails, lets Incus
place instances on it. Needs `manage-infrastructure`; audited.

delete.summary:
Withdraws an approval: revokes the machine's unused join token. Needs
`manage-infrastructure`; audited.

post.summary:
Approves a machine: asks Incus for its single-use join token, returned only in this
response with the command to run on the server. Needs `manage-infrastructure`; audited
without the token.

get.summary: Networks in all projects. Needs `read-inventory`.

Read-only readiness checks of the Incus server or cluster and of the projects Apelora
deploys into. Changes nothing. Needs `read-inventory`.
Incus projects. Needs `read-inventory`.
Open sessions the caller started, and those on applications they may operate.

delete.summary:
Ends a session now. Allowed for the person who has it and for whoever may operate its
application. Anything else answers 404.

get.summary: Storage pools. Needs `read-inventory`.

Versions of this control plane and the Incus release it is pinned to, and when the
certificates Apelora uses to reach Incus expire. Needs `read-inventory`. The running Incus
version is in `/api/v1/health`.
API tokens, active and revoked (never the tokens themselves). Needs `manage-tokens`.

post.summary: Creates an API token, shown only in this response. Needs `manage-tokens`.

delete.summary: Revokes an API token; it stops working at once. Needs `manage-tokens`.

get.summary: Who is calling, with the role assignments and permissions in force.

observed.description: Incus could be read just now. When false, `items` is empty and nothing may be opened.

reason.description: Why not, in a sentence the interface can show.

admissible.description: No check failed: the machine can be admitted.

actions.description: What the caller may do now, from their permissions and the application's state.

icon.description: Key of the icon (a catalog icon such as `nginx`, or a generic one such as `generic-box`).

observedAt.description: When Incus was observed for these statuses (RFC 3339), and whether that failed.

services.description: Allocated service addresses (empty without a database or service range).

after.description: What they could do once this assignment exists (the new grant has the nil assignment id).

allowed.description: Could the signed-in administrator save this assignment?

before.description: What the person can already do at that scope.

inert.description: Permissions in the role that do nothing at this scope.

actor.description: Stable id of who acted, e.g. `user:<uuid>`, `service:<uuid>`, `token:<name>`.

scope.description: The organisation, project and application the event concerns, when it concerns any.

Availability.description: How a module may be run and recovered (from its catalog class).

Capabilities.description: What a provisioner can do to a machine without someone at the server.

certificate.description:
`deploy` (restricted client identity), `admin` (unrestricted client identity) or
`server` (the pinned Incus server certificate).

daysLeft.description: Whole days left; negative once expired.

Class.description:
What kind of power a permission is. Only `Tenant` permissions can be granted below the
platform level, so an organisation or project role can never reach physical servers,
the Incus cluster or the platform's own security settings.

ClusterMember.description: Observed state of an Incus cluster member ("minion" in the UI).

scheduler.description:
Incus's `scheduler.instance` for this member: `all` (the default), `manual` (only
instances targeted at it are placed there) or `group`.

members.description: Empty when the Incus server is not clustered.

environments.description: The grant counts only for resources in environments of these kinds.

requireMfa.description: The grant counts only when the caller signed in with multi-factor authentication.

confirm.description: The member's name again, typed by the administrator.

force.description:
Evacuate although the dry run found blockers (a workload may lose service). Needs the
unsafe-evacuation permission and an approval from another person.

confirm.description: The snapshot's name again, typed by the person restoring it.
The volume's Incus name again, typed by the person deleting it.

Connection.description: One connection of the design: `from` may reach `to` (module ids).

port.description: `None`: any port of the transport (the protocol has no well-known port).

document.description: The first draft (a Studio document), if any.

environmentId.description: The environment (and so the project) the application lives in.

name.description:
Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter; at most 40 characters. Fixed
for the life of the application (instances are named after it).

memberName.description: Name the new member will join with.

name.description: Who or what uses it, e.g. "ci" or a person's name.

connections.description: The design's connections; enforced when the control plane has a network uplink.

document.description: The Studio document, saved as an immutable revision. Ignored when `version` is given.

published.description: Ports reachable from outside the application (needs connections to be enforced).

removeMissing.description: Also delete the application's instances that are no longer in the design.

version.description:
Deploy this published version (its stored document) instead of saving `document` as a
new revision. Drafts can never be deployed.

networkJob.description: The job that applies the connections to the application's network, when enforced.

plan.description: The plan that was applied (recomputed when applying).

deployedVersion.description: The published version the application was last deployed from.

observedAt.description: When the control plane last observed Incus for this answer (RFC 3339).

stale.description: The answer could not be refreshed (Incus unreachable); the status is `unknown`.

hasUnpublishedChanges.description: The draft has changes that no published version contains.

DesiredModule.description: One module of the design, turned into the instances it should run as.

guestOs.description: The operating system inside (from the class): decides which sessions it offers.

internet.description: What it may reach outside the application (enforced with the connections).

module.description: The module's stable id in the design (e.g. `nginx-01`).

replicas.description: How many instances (1–9); more than one only for stateless modules.

spec.description: Image, kind and settings; the control plane sets the name, project and owner.

grants.description: Where each part of this permission comes from.

reason.description: Why; at least 10 characters. Recorded in the audit trail.

EnvKind.description: Kind of environment; policies such as "production needs MFA" refer to it.

incusProject.description: The restricted Incus project this environment deploys into.

incusProjectConfig.description:
The settings that project needs (restricted, unprivileged, no host devices). Apelora does
not create or verify the Incus project yet: an administrator does, with these settings.

ErrorBody.description: Error body for every non-2xx response.

EvacuationItem.description: One instance on the member being evacuated.

impact.description: What it means for the application while the member is evacuated.

outcome.description: What Incus will do with it.

blocked.description: Why evacuating now is refused; empty when it may proceed.

targets.description: Members that can take instances (online, other than this one).

viaGroup.description: Set when the grant reaches the caller through a group.

externalName.description: The group's name in the identity provider's tokens, when members come from there.

sizeMib.description: The new size in MiB; at least the current one (volumes only grow).

GuestOs.description: The operating system inside a module, from its catalog class (never guessed from names).

HealthState.description: The decided health of an instance.

IdentityProjectList.description:
Identity projects (`/api/v1/identity/projects`); not the Incus projects of
`/api/v1/projects`, whose schema is `ProjectList`.

ImageSource.description: Where an instance's root image comes from.

alias.description:
Alias such as `debian/13` or, for OCI, `repository:tag`. Pin an OCI image by digest:
`repository@sha256:<64 hex digits>`.

fingerprint.description:
Pins a simplestreams image: the full SHA-256 fingerprint Incus gives it. The instance
must then be built from exactly this image.

server.description: Image server URL, e.g. a simplestreams server or an OCI registry.

IncusStatus.description: What the control plane knows about its Incus connection.

connected.description: True only when talking to a real Incus server (never for mock data).

Instance.description: Observed state of one Incus instance.

evacuate.description:
What Incus does with it when its member is evacuated (`cluster.evacuate`, with
profiles applied); `None`: Incus's default, `auto`.

managed.description: Carries Apelora's ownership marker: only these can be stopped or deleted through Apelora.

oneOf.description: The application and module this instance was deployed for (Apelora's labels).

unreachable.description:
Incus cannot report its configuration because its member is unreachable, so its
labels (and `managed`, `owner`) are unknown, not absent.

InstanceAction.description: A state change Apelora can request for one of its instances.

detail.description: What the decision rests on, e.g. `port check failing`.

restartedAt.description: RFC 3339: when the worker last restarted it for failing its check.

since.description: RFC 3339: since when it has had this health.

InstanceKind.description: Kind of Incus instance as reported by the cluster.

InstanceSpec.description: An instance Apelora should create. Apelora's ownership marker is added on creation.

architectures.description:
Architectures the image is known to run on (see [`ARCHITECTURES`]); empty allows any.
Checked against the cluster before creating and against the instance Incus created.

config.description: Extra instance config; keys under `user.apelora.` are reserved.

oneOf.description:
Set by the control plane when the application's connections are enforced: the NIC
joins the application's network with its own ACL (unmatched traffic rejected).
Set by the control plane when the instance is part of an application deployment.

profiles.description: Profiles to apply, in order; empty applies the project's `default` profile.

volumes.description: Persistent volumes, each created for this instance on the member it runs on.

Internet.description:
What a module may reach outside the application (the internet, through the uplink).
Inside the application only connections count, whatever this says.

incusOperation.description: The Incus operation the current attempt is waiting on, if any.

created.description: False when an earlier request with the same idempotency key already created the job.

token.description: Single-use secret for `incus admin init` on the new server. Shown only in this response.

warnings.description: E.g. that the token lives longer than recommended.

KindAccess.description: What a person may open on one instance, with the reason when not.

approvalRequired.description: Another person must approve first (production). The request goes through `/approvals`.

reason.description: Why it is not available (permission, state, set-up). Absent when allowed.

Level.description: How wide a scope is. Lower is wider. `Pool` is a separate branch under the platform.

approvalExpiresAt.description: When the approval's join token stops working, as Incus reported it.

capabilities.description: What the provider can do without someone at the server.

memberStatus.description: The cluster member's status (`Online`, `Offline`, `Evacuated`…) once it has joined.

enrolCommand.description: What to run on the server; it asks for the token without echoing it.

token.description: Single-use join token for the enrolment script. Shown only in this response.

MachineState.description: Where a machine is in enrolment. Derived from the record and from Incus, never stored.

operation.description: Incus operation carrying out the evacuation or restore.

oneOf.description:
What the worker decided from the instance's port check, with hysteresis; absent for
instances that are not checked (no service address, not running, or no database).

MovePlan.description: What the move does, decided before anything changes.

blocked.description: Why the move is refused; empty when it may proceed.

copyMib.description: How much data is copied while it is stopped, in MiB.

stops.description: Stops for the move (and starts again on the new member if it was running).

volumes.description: Volumes copied to the new member, then deleted on the old one once it runs there.

confirm.description: The instance's name again, typed by the person moving it.

locations.description: Cluster members it is created on; empty when not per member (or unknown).

NetworkAttachment.description: Where an instance's NIC is attached: the application's network, with its own ACL.

uplink.description: Uplink network the application network is created on.

action.description: The permission to be exercised, e.g. `hardware.delete`.

target.description: What it will be done to, e.g. `machine:rack1-07`.

expiresAt.description: RFC 3339. Assignments may expire; emergency grants must.

incusProject.description: Platform administrators only: map an existing Incus project instead of the derived name.

expiresInDays.description: Automation identities only: days until their token expires (1–365, default 90).

confirmDisruption.description:
Required to stop or restart an application that has single-instance or stateful
modules: it acknowledges that their clients lose service meanwhile.

created.description: False when the same `Idempotency-Key` had already created it.

Owner.description: The application and module an instance belongs to.

PendingJoin.description: A join token that has been issued and not yet used, revoked or expired (no secret).

floor.description: The narrowest scope level at which a grant takes effect.

warnings.description: Facts the designer should know before applying, e.g. single points of failure.

module.description: The module in the design (for `remove`: the label of the instance being removed).

reason.description: Why, in a sentence (e.g. what the conflicting instance is).

connections.description: The design's connections; enforced when the control plane has a network uplink.

published.description: Ports reachable from outside the application (needs connections to be enforced).

overall.description: The worst status among the checks.

restricted.description: `restricted=true`: the project limits what its instances may do.

ProviderMode.description: Where the backend's view of the infrastructure comes from.

ProvisionerKind.description: What installs and powers a machine. Every provisioner enrols the same way.

label.description: A short name for the version, e.g. `after load test`.

Published.description:
A port of a module reachable from outside the application (in the Studio: connected
from a gateway). Only ports with a number can be published.

name.description: The name it will have as a cluster member.

blocked.description: Why removing it now is refused; empty when it may proceed.

Role.description:
Who may do what. Every API route names the permission it needs; roles map to permissions
here and nowhere else.

scopes.description: Scope levels it can be assigned at.

baseVersion.description: The draft version this edit started from; omit only for the first save.

oneOf.description: A named group of physical machines (a MAAS resource pool, if MAAS is adopted).

ServerInfo.description: Facts about the Incus server the adapter is talking to.

architectures.description: Architectures this server can run (`environment.architectures`); empty when unknown.

token.description: The API token of an automation identity, shown only here.

apiAccess.description: Can call the Apelora API (automation identities only).

credentialRef.description: Name of the credential in the backend's secret store (never the secret).

operations.description: The operation families this kind may perform.

ServiceStatus.description: A stateless module's service address: a load balancer over its healthy replicas.

SessionKind.description: What a person can open on a module.

connectPath.description: Path of the websocket, relative to the API.

provider.description: Where the instance lives: a `mock` provider's sessions talk to a labelled fake shell.

ticket.description:
Shown once. Present it as the `ticket.<value>` sub-protocol when opening the websocket;
never put it in a URL.

consistency.description:
`crash-consistent` when an instance was running, else `stopped`: a snapshot of a
running database is what a power cut would leave behind.

Source.description: Where inventory data came from and when it was read.

locations.description: Cluster members it is created on; empty when unknown.

SystemInfo.description: Facts about this control plane and the Incus release it is pinned to.

certificates.description: The certificates Apelora uses to reach Incus and when they expire (empty with the mock).

incusPinned.description: Incus release Apelora is tested against (`upstream.lock.yaml`).

incusSeries.description: Incus LTS series the pin follows, e.g. "7.0".

token.description: The token itself, shown only in this response.

VolumeClass.description:
The policy a volume is created under. Only `data-local` exists so far: persistent, one
writer, on the member's own pool; moving it means stopping the instance.

VolumeContent.description: What the volume holds: a mounted filesystem or a raw disk (virtual machines only).

incusName.description: The Incus volume (`<instance>-<name>`): what to type to delete it.

member.description: Member of a member-local pool; empty on a standalone server.

VolumeMount.description: A volume a module asks for.

name.description: Name in the design, e.g. `data`: lowercase letters, digits and `-`, at most 16.

path.description: Where a filesystem volume is mounted inside the instance; none for a block volume.

pool.description: The pool the class resolves to. Set by the control plane, never by a caller.

VolumeUse.description: What Incus reports about a recorded volume now.

capabilities.description: Permission ids held at some scope (what the UI may offer; the server decides each request).

deployProjects.description: Incus projects this control plane deploys into (`APELORA_DEPLOY_PROJECTS`).

id.description: The user or service identity id; absent for legacy tokens.

permissions.description: What the older, coarse permissions amount to for this caller at platform level.

platformPermissions.description: Permission ids held across the whole platform.

oneOf.description: The role of a legacy API token; `null` for people and service identities.

roles.description: The role assignments in force for this caller.

bearer.description: An OIDC access token from the identity provider, an automation service token (`aps_…`) or a legacy API token (`apl_…`).
